subject: Analytix renewal: Q2 usage spike analysis & proposed capacity uplift
messages:
From: Sofia Marin <sofia.marin@analytix.ai>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Q2 renewal review — unexpected token spike

Hi Neha,

Hope you had a good weekend. We're looking at our Q2 bill and seeing a ~2.6x spike in token usage in mid-June compared to May. Before our renewal conversation next week, can you:

- Share a short breakdown of where the tokens were spent (per-route or per-model if available)
- Any quick explanation for the spike (we suspect batch generation for our model eval jobs)
- Options for smoothing costs / reserving capacity if we expect more of these evaluation bursts going forward

We want to avoid surprises for our finance team and are open to a capacity uplift if it makes sense.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if that’s easier.

Best,
Sofia Marin
Head of Data Science | Analytix.ai
Sofia.Marin@analytix.ai

---
Attachment: (none)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Marin <sofia.marin@analytix.ai>, renewals@analytix.ai
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@analytix.ai>
Date: 2026-07-11T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q2 renewal review — unexpected token spike

Hi Sofia — thanks for the heads up and the context. I dug into the Q2 logs and attached two artifacts: a CSV with per-route token breakdown and a short ROI summary that maps the spike to customer value. Quick summary below: 

- Root cause: a scheduled model-evaluation job (internal codename: batch-eval-v2) ran across ~1.2M examples on 2026-06-14, triggering large generation calls over a four-hour window.
- Distribution: ~72% of the incremental tokens were from the /generate endpoint using the 7B-opt model; remaining from embeddings for search re-indexing.
- Cost impact: incremental spend for June ~ $18.4k; normalized monthly run-rate (without batch) ~ $6.9k.
- Mitigations already in place: prefix caching reduced repeat token costs by ~15% for the evaluation retries; we also flagged the job to throttle in future runs.

Options I recommend: 
1) Reserved uplift: add a dedicated pool (2x S-4 GPUs) as a reserved burst capacity for scheduled jobs — reduces per-token unit cost and guarantees throughput.
2) Term change: move from 12→18 months with a modest commit increase; this gives us room to offer a volume-based discount on the reserved GPUs.
3) Short-term credit: we can offer a one-time usage credit to smooth the Q2 bump while you transition to reserved capacity.

Attached: analytix_usage_Q2_2026.csv, analytix_roi_summary.pdf

If that aligns, can we schedule a 30-min call to confirm target reserved size and proposed price? My availability tomorrow 11:00–13:00 PT and Thursday 09:00–11:00 PT.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

---
Attachments: analytix_usage_Q2_2026.csv (CSV, 42KB), analytix_roi_summary.pdf (PDF, 270KB)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-11T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Q2 renewal review — unexpected token spike (Analytix)

Folks — forwarding the client thread and the attached usage/ROI. TL;DR: scheduled eval job caused a one-off token spike; client is open to reserving capacity and prefers an 18-month term if we can be flexible on monthly commit pricing.

Proposed internal ask:
- Offer: +2 S-4 reserved GPUs (baseline for scheduled batch windows)
- Term: 18 months, with a 10% list discount on the reserved capacity line and a one-time $7k usage credit against June consumption
- Rationale: preserves revenue visibility, reduces unit cost for client, positions us to upsell to a larger dedicated pool next renewal if bursts persist

Questions for pricing/legal:
- Is 10% on reserved pool within manager-approved exceptions?
- Do we need a cost-cap clause for ad-hoc burst beyond reserved capacity? (client asked about smoothing bursts)

Connor — can you run high-level math on blended unit economics and confirm whether we should push a commit floor (e.g., $30k/mo) vs. pure per-GPU pricing? Evelyn — if you can flag any compliance/terms implications for the 18-month term and the credit, that would be great.

Thanks,
Neha

---
(Internal only, no extra attachments)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-12T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Q2 renewal review — unexpected token spike (Analytix)

Thanks Neha — quick thoughts:

- 10% discount on reserved pool is probably OK but let's structure it as a tiered commit:
  - Tier 1 (baseline): $30k/mo commit -> 8% discount
  - Tier 2 (preferred): $45k/mo commit -> 12% discount
  That gives us room to upsell and protects unit economics.
- Instead of a hard cost-cap, propose an overage rate that is 1.5x hosted list for ad-hoc bursts beyond reserved capacity. We document recommended throttles in the runbook and offer help re-scheduling heavy jobs.
- Approve $7k credit as a one-time concession tied to execution of the 18-month term and the reserved pool order.

Neha — if you share a projected monthly spend table for both the baseline and burst months, I can finalize margin impact and sign-off. Evelyn — can you confirm there are no odd legal flags on the commit tiers / credit language?

Cheers,
Connor
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-07-15T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal proposal and next steps — Analytix (DEAL-7425)

Hi Sofia / Tom — thanks again for the quick sync earlier this week. Per our conversation and internal alignment, here is the proposal we can put into a renewal/commit: 

Summary: 
- Term: 18 months (starting upon signature)
- Reserved capacity: 2 x S-4 GPUs dedicated for scheduled batch windows
- Commit: $30k/mo baseline -> tier structure available to move to $45k/mo for additional discount
- One-time credit: $7,000 applied to June 2026 invoice upon signature
- Overage: 1.5x hosted list unit rate for any ad-hoc bursts beyond reserved capacity; Redwood will provide a short runbook to help re-schedule heavy jobs and recommend caching/batching tweaks

Next steps: 
1) I’ll send a DocuSign with the 18-month amendment and reserved capacity addendum (link below). Please review and sign when ready: https://www.docusign.com/analytix/renewal/DEAL-7425
2) On signature, we’ll schedule a kickoff with our infra team to set up the reserved pool and provide an operational runbook (target: within 5 business days of signing).

I’ve re-attached the ROI summary for your finance team and the usage CSV for reference. If you want any changes to the commit/tiers before we convert to DocuSign, say the word and we’ll re-run the math.

Thanks — looking forward to continuing the partnership.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
